note: Every row below was read directly from an official Kalshi source on 2026-11-22 UTC (S25-S27 were added in the repository-review pass of the same date). Third-party pages are never used as a source for a factual claim on this site.

sources.claim: Demo REST base URL is https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 (recommended) and https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 is also supported. Production is https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2.
Golf is a tag (subcategory) inside the Sports category. Full category→tag map retrieved from the live API.
The monthly US gas price series is KXAAAGASM: primary category Economics, categories [Economics, Commodities], tags [Oil and energy, Oil & Gas], one event per month with one market per strike.
sources.publisher: Kalshi documentation — worked example in the glossary

sources.claim: Settlement: a YES outcome pays $1 per YES contract, a NO outcome pays $1 per NO contract; only net positions settle.

Order placement uses POST /portfolio/events/orders (Create Order V2) with ticker, side, count, price, time_in_force, self_trade_prevention_type and an optional client_order_id; `side` is the book side (bid = yes, ask = no), count is a fixed-point string and price a fixed-point dollar string; HTTP 201 means accepted, not necessarily resting.

Rate limits are token buckets per tier; most requests cost 10 tokens; GET /portfolio/balance has its own bucket of 1–5 requests per second; unauthenticated public requests are limited separately and 429s should be retried with backoff.

The ticker WebSocket channel sends price_dollars, yes_bid_dollars, yes_ask_dollars, volume_fp, open_interest_fp, yes_bid_size_fp, yes_ask_size_fp, last_trade_size_fp and ts_ms, flushed about once per second per changed market.
WebSocket connections use the same Kalshi API-key authentication, subscribe via {"id":1,"cmd":"subscribe","params":{"channels":[…],"market_tickers":[…]}}, and must resubscribe after a reconnect.
GET /portfolio/balance returns balance (cents), balance_dollars and portfolio_value (cents), updated_ts, and a per-exchange-index balance_breakdown.
GET /portfolio/positions returns market_positions with ticker, position_fp (positive = YES, negative = NO), market_exposure_dollars, realized_pnl_dollars, fees_paid_dollars and total_traded_dollars.
Fees are executed at six-decimal dollar granularity with round-up behaviour and a rounding-fee accumulator; direct members settle balances to $0.0001, non-direct members to $0.01.
Demo WebSocket URL is wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2; wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 is also supported. Production is wss://external-api-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2.
The demo environment is https://demo.kalshi.co, uses mock funds, has credentials separate from production, and Kalshi warns that demo prices and behaviour may not reflect real markets.
A demo account is created by the account holder at demo.kalshi.co/sign-up, is not preloaded with funds, and accepts test payment methods; demo credentials are separate from production.
REST market data is cached briefly, so prices, sizes and status can lag the exchange by several seconds; WebSockets are the documented mechanism for current prices.
OpenAPI spec lists four supported servers: external-api.kalshi.com, api.elections.kalshi.com, external-api.demo.kalshi.co and demo-api.kalshi.co, all under /trade-api/v2.
GET /exchange/status returns exchange_active, trading_active and per-exchange-index statuses. Live demo read on 2026-11-22 returned exchange_active=true, trading_active=true across four indexes.

Live production read on 2026-11-22: GET /markets?series_ticker=KXAAAGASM&status=open returned strikes 3.45 / 3.55 / 3.65 with prices, volume_fp and open_interest_fp; GET /series?tags=Golf returned KXPGAEAGLE, KXLIVR1LEAD and KXRYDERCUPCAPTAIN among others.
Authenticated requests carry KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE and KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP. The signed text is timestamp + HTTP method + request path, excluding the query string and host.
RSA keys sign with RSA-PSS and SHA-256; Ed25519 keys sign the message directly. Signatures are base64 in KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE; the timestamp is Unix milliseconds.
Public market-data endpoints (series, events, markets, orderbook) require no API key.

Market objects expose yes_bid_dollars, yes_ask_dollars, no_bid_dollars, no_ask_dollars, last_price_dollars, previous_price_dollars, volume_fp, volume_24h_fp, open_interest_fp, yes_bid_size_fp, yes_ask_size_fp, status, result, close_time and rules_primary.

Orderbook responses contain only bids: orderbook_fp.yes_dollars and orderbook_fp.no_dollars as [price_dollars, count_fp] pairs sorted ascending; the best bid is the last element; asks are implied as $1.00 − the opposite side's bid.
Candlesticks: GET /series/{series_ticker}/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks with start_ts and end_ts in seconds and period_interval of 1, 60 or 1440 minutes; at most 5,000 periods per request.

A series has one primary category, a categories discovery list and a tags subcategory list. The category filter matches any entry in categories. Official categories include Elections, Crypto, Entertainment, Sports, Economics and Commodities.

Trading fees are roundup(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1 - P)) for taker fills and roundup(M x 0.0175 x C x P x (1 - P)) for maker fills, where P is the contract price in dollars and M a per-series multiplier. The published table gives $0.02 for one contract at $0.50 and $1.75 for 100 contracts at $0.50. Schedule effective 2026-07-07.

Timestamp filters on GET /markets are only valid with specific status values: min_close_ts with status=closed and min_settled_ts with status=settled. Status `settled` in the REST filter corresponds to the terminal `finalized` market status.
